items.markdown: Fig. 1 | α-Syn aggregates alter mitochondrial morphology. Morphological analysis of TOMM20 positive mitochondria using plug-in thresholded images (bottom panels) generated from original raw images (top panels) for SH-SY5Y neuronal cells (a) and HMC3 microglial cells (b). Relative abundance of major observable mitochondrial phenotype depicted by the cartoon below. (c-d) Morphological quantifications of mitochondrial numbers (count), perimeter, area, form factor, and aspect ratio per cell for neuronal cells (c) and microglial cells (d). N = 3 independent experiments, n = 50 cells. Statistical significance was calculated using one-sided Brown-Forsythe and Welch ANOVA tests with Dunnett’s T3 multiple comparison. To indicate p-values in a compact manner, the following representation paradigm is used: control = X, CCCP = Y and α-Syn-treatment = Z. For c—mitochondrial count: X-Y and X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean mitochondrial perimeter: X-Y: p = 1.92x10<sup>−9</sup>, X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean mitochondria area: X-Y: p = 3.27x10<sup>−6</sup>; X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean form factor: X-Y and X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean aspect ratio: X-Y: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>, X-Z: p = 1.91x10<sup>−8</sup>. For d—mitochondrial count: X-Y: p = 2.61x10<sup>−6</sup>, X-Z: p = 1.207x10<sup>−5</sup>; mean mitochondrial perimeter: X-Y and X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean mitochondrial area: X-Y and X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean form factor: X-Y and X-Z: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>; mean aspect ratio: X-Y: p < 1x10<sup>−15</sup>, X-Z: p = 4.798×10<sup>−12</sup>. Data represented as median and quartiles, with mean values mentioned within the graphs. For form factor and aspect ratio, AU=arbitrary units. A schematic representation of mitochondria was created in BioRender. MAYA, S. (2026) https://BioRender.com/cot8ver.

Mitochondrial depolarization has been demonstrated to be associated with the release of Cytochrome c, an intermembrane space protein<sup>47</sup>, although depolarization can occur significantly later than Cytochrome c release into the cytoplasm<sup>48</sup>. To determine whether the observed loss in neuronal and microglial ΔΨm was also accompanied by Cytochrome c release, we performed co-immunostaining with

TOMM20 (Fig. 2d, e). We observed significant Cytochrome c release in both cell types upon exposure to α-Syn aggregates (Fig. 2f, i), accompanied by elevated cytosolic levels (Fig. 2g, j) and a reduction in overall Cytochrome c protein levels (Fig. 2h, k). Taken together, these results are indicative of outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) and functional impairment of mitochondria following α-Syn exposure.
